cards.back: After striking an unattended vehicle, locate and notify its owner immediately; if that is impossible, leave a conspicuous note with your name, address and insurer.

cards.back: The handbook lists uninsured-driving fines of one hundred fifty dollars for a first violation and three hundred dollars for a further violation within three years, with possible suspension.

cards.back: After a no-insurance conviction, the handbook requires insurance proof for one year and a restricted replacement license, with fifty-dollar fees both for that replacement and for later removing the restriction.

cards.front: What words complete the handbook rule: “Use nine-one-one for emergency blank weather or road-condition information.”?

cards.back: At low speed, gently check braking traction and adjust driving speed to the available grip.

cards.front: What words complete the handbook rule: “The handbook allows studded blank through April fifteenth.”?
cards.back: The handbook allows studded snow tires from October fifteenth through April fifteenth.

cards.front: What words complete the handbook rule: “Passing trucks can create a cloud of snow blank speed and watch the road and following traffic.”?
cards.back: Passing trucks can create a cloud of snow that sharply reduces visibility; reduce speed and watch the road and following traffic.

cards.front: What words complete the handbook rule: “Bridges and shaded pavement blank longer than nearby roadway.”?

cards.front: What words complete the handbook rule: “With antilock brakes, maintain firm continuous blank or repeatedly releasing the pedal.”?

cards.front: What words complete the handbook rule: “Carry winter emergency supplies, blank shovel and energy food.”?
cards.back: Carry winter emergency supplies, including warm clothes, footwear, a shovel and energy food.

cards.front: What words complete the handbook rule: “When stranded in a blank rather than wandering away.”?

cards.front: What words complete the handbook rule: “Keep well behind a snowplow because it may stop, blank and its driver cannot see directly behind it.”?
cards.back: Keep well behind a snowplow because it may stop, reverse or throw sanding material, and its driver cannot see directly behind it.

cards.front: What words complete the handbook rule: “On a multilane road, a plow may blank shoulder, so establish its location before proceeding.”?
cards.back: On a multilane road, a plow may occupy either lane or the shoulder, so establish its location before proceeding.

cards.front: What words complete the handbook rule: “Snowdrifts can push blank requires exceptional caution.”?
cards.back: Snowdrifts can push a plow sideways; passing it requires exceptional caution.

cards.front: What words complete the handbook rule: “Do not drive into a snow whiteout; blank a safe opportunity exists to pass.”?
cards.back: Do not drive into a snow whiteout; wait until visibility returns and a safe opportunity exists to pass.

cards.front: What words complete the handbook rule: “A road that looks sanded may blank can sink into packed snow.”?

cards.front: What words complete the handbook rule: “Reduce speed on slippery blank of a skid.”?
cards.back: Reduce speed on slippery roads to lower the risk of a skid.

cards.back: For the handbook's rear-wheel-drive skid procedure, stay off the brakes, ease off acceleration gradually and steer in the direction the rear is sliding.

cards.front: What words complete the handbook rule: “New rain combines with road blank an especially slippery surface.”?
cards.back: New rain combines with road oil and dirt to create an especially slippery surface.

cards.front: What words complete the handbook rule: “Hydroplaning occurs when tires blank contacting the road.”?
cards.back: Hydroplaning occurs when tires ride on water rather than contacting the road.

cards.front: What words complete the handbook rule: “Rain reduces visibility and blank speed and close attention.”?
cards.back: Rain reduces visibility and raises skid risk, requiring slower speed and close attention.

cards.front: What words complete the handbook rule: “Turn around rather than drive blank when the water looks shallow.”?
cards.back: Turn around rather than drive across a flooded road, even when the water looks shallow.

cards.front: What words complete the handbook rule: “Floodwater can conceal dips blank making apparent depth unreliable.”?
cards.back: Floodwater can conceal dips or a washed-out road foundation, making apparent depth unreliable.

cards.front: What words complete the handbook rule: “The handbook warns that six inches of water blank underside and cause stalling or loss of control.”?
cards.back: The handbook warns that six inches of water can reach most passenger cars' underside and cause stalling or loss of control.

cards.front: What words complete the handbook rule: “Two feet of moving water can sweep blank and sport-utility vehicles, according to the handbook.”?
cards.back: Two feet of moving water can sweep away most vehicles, including pickups and sport-utility vehicles, according to the handbook.

cards.front: What words complete the handbook rule: “When floodwater blocks the only route, blank wait for it to recede.”?
cards.back: When floodwater blocks the only route, go to higher ground and wait for it to recede.

cards.front: What words complete the handbook rule: “A tire failure may produce thumping; front-tire failure blank while a rear failure may cause swaying.”?
cards.back: A tire failure may produce thumping; front-tire failure pulls toward the damaged side, while a rear failure may cause swaying.

cards.front: What words complete the handbook rule: “After a blowout, grip the wheel, steer straight and ease off blank before braking, then move to the shoulder when nearly stopped.”?
cards.back: After a blowout, grip the wheel, steer straight and ease off acceleration; wait for full control before braking, then move to the shoulder when nearly stopped.

cards.front: What words complete the handbook rule: “If a tire drops onto the shoulder, do not blank regain control, check behind, signal and return gently.”?
cards.back: If a tire drops onto the shoulder, do not swerve back; ease off acceleration, regain control, check behind, signal and return gently.

cards.front: What words complete the handbook rule: “If headlights fail, try parking lights and blank leave the roadway as soon as possible.”?
cards.back: If headlights fail, try parking lights and turn signals, slow down and leave the roadway as soon as possible.

cards.front: What words complete the handbook rule: “For a stuck accelerator, disengage the clutch or blank safely; never select the ignition-lock position while moving.”?
cards.back: For a stuck accelerator, disengage the clutch or select neutral and steer off safely; never select the ignition-lock position while moving.

cards.front: What words complete the handbook rule: “Switching off the engine blank steering and brakes.”?
cards.back: Switching off the engine can remove power assistance for steering and brakes.

cards.front: What words complete the handbook rule: “Slow for ruts, holes, blank abrupt braking or steering.”?
cards.back: Slow for ruts, holes, broken pavement and gravel, avoiding abrupt braking or steering.

cards.front: What words complete the handbook rule: “If an oncoming vehicle enters your lane, slow and flash headlights; if blank leave the road or stop on the far-right shoulder when conditions permit.”?
cards.back: If an oncoming vehicle enters your lane, slow and flash headlights; if it continues, move right and leave the road or stop on the far-right shoulder when conditions permit.

cards.front: What words complete the handbook rule: “Texting while driving is prohibited, and the handbook blank the described distracting activity that impairs safe control.”?
cards.back: Texting while driving is prohibited, and the handbook lists a one-hundred-dollar penalty for the described distracting activity that impairs safe control.

cards.front: What words complete the handbook rule: “Hold the wheel with both hands, using one blank to avoid riding and overheating the brakes.”?

cards.back: Sleep is the safe remedy for sleepiness behind the wheel; continuing tired increases collision risk.
